data.name: Bhakti
data.gender_notes: Bhakti is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Bhakti refers to the deep love and devotion towards a personal deity or a god. It is a state of selfless and intense attachment, and is considered the purest form of worship in Hinduism. The name Bhakti carries the meaning “Devotion, Love” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bhakti usually hope their child will grow to embody devotion, love and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A spiritual journey towards self-realization and union with the divine.
data.etymology: Bhakti belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Devotion, Love.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bhakti total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_sanskrit.name: भक्ति
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: भज् (to serve) + ति (end or goal) = भक्ति (devotion, love for God)

in_hindi.name: भक्ति
in_hindi.long_meaning: भजन (to serve) + ति (तक) = भक्ति (प्रेम, ईश्वर के लिए भक्ति)

in_tamil.name: பக்தி
in_tamil.long_meaning: பகிர் (to serve) + தி (தொல்லை) = பக்தி (ஆத்மாவிசயம், தூவர்கள் இருக்கும் ஆட்டம்)

in_telugu.name: భక్తి
in_telugu.long_meaning: భజ్ (to serve) + తి (అభ్యర్ధిచేది) = భక్తి (దేశికేయోదేశముదే, ధోయేశ్వర చేది)

data.cultural_impact: Bhakti has had a profound impact on Indian culture, shaping the way in which spirituality is practiced and expressed. Bhakti poetry and music have been a significant part of Indian literature and art, with famous compositions like the Bhagavad Gita and the works of the Alwars and Nayanars inspiring millions. Bhakti has also influenced Indian social fabric, promoting the idea of Lord as a loving and caring father, approachable and accessible to all, irrespective of caste, creed, or social position.
data.spiritual_significance: Bhakti is considered a powerful spiritual path in Hinduism, offering the seeker a direct and personal connection with the divine. It is believed that through bhakti, the devotee experiences the grace and love of the deity, leading to spiritual growth and enlightenment. Bhakti is also considered a balance to the more intellectual and cerebral forms of spirituality, offering a more emotional and heartfelt connection to the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bhakti represents the deep, selfless love and devotion towards a personal deity or God. It is the emotional bond between the individual soul and the divine, fostering inner peace and spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Bhakti is a Sanskrit term that refers to devotion to a personal deity. The name Bhakti carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Bhakti is a central concept in Hinduism and is expressed through various forms of worship, including poetry, music, and rituals.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Bhakti remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.

name_in_real_life.story: Lakshmi Bhakti, a teacher in Mumbai, India, shares that their name Bhakti meaning "Devotion, Love" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.
